sar.narrative: The cardholder identified as customer C07987 was linked to visa credit card C07987-K2. On 2016-12-01 at 17:28:53 an online purchase of $99.92 was authorized on product code R using device profile Windows | other | chrome 61.0 | 1280x720. The transaction originated from billing region 264 and was recorded under transaction ID 3503878. Investigation revealed that the same rare device profile had been employed on four other cards (C01104-K2, C01983-K1, C06224-K2, C11309-K1) within the prior 30 days, with three of those transactions matching the amount range of this purchase. The pattern was classified as card-not-present activity from a new device, a scenario that has been 10.7 times more common in confirmed fraud than in normal online traffic. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transaction, did not share the card details, and still possessed the card. Because the purchase was made by an unauthorized party on the cardholder's account, the activity was deemed suspicious and resulted in the card being blocked, the case created, a report filed, and connected cards placed under monitoring.

stop_reason: The customer's reply settled the question (section 6): probability moved from 0.70 to 0.96 and the episode (1 transaction(s), $99.92) is scoped. Further steps would not change the actions.
